Subject 6th District Silk Filature Workers' Union -
new committee members assume office

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by [签名]

The new standing committee members of the 6th
District Silk Filature Workers' Union, 1 Min Teh Li, Tatung
Road, Chapei, assumed office in the afternoon of November 28

meeting, the following resolutions were passed :-

Silk Trade Control Committee of the Chekiang Province to
revise the measures for the control of the trade.
(The Union alleges that the Control Committee has limited
the transportation of cocoons to other provinces, and that
the procedure has resulted in a number of local filatures
being compelled to suspend operations).
2. That arrangements be made to establish a school for the
children of employees of silk filatures.
3. That endeavours be made to induce employers of silk
filatures to grant an increase of wages to their workers.

Sir,

Subject Labour Dispute at Tsung Yah Silk Factory, 366 Alcock Rd,

Made by D.S. Hillhouse. Forwarded by

Sir,
With reference to a letter received at this station on
13.6.36 from the workers of the Tsung Yah Silk Factory, 366
Alcock Road, the translation of which is attached, D.S.I. Tseu
Kwei Sung and the undersigned proceeded to the above factory
at 10 a.m. 13.6.36 when two of the workers who signed the letter
were located and consented to come to the station to allow
further enquiries to be made. When questioned in the presence
of D.S.I. Cumming, the two workers named Sung Fong Hai (沈方海)
and Yih Mau Er (叶毛儿), admitted that the contents of the
letter were incorrect and that actually none of the property
had been removed from the factory on 12.6.36. They stated that
C.D.S. 224( the detective referred to by them in the letter),
arrived at the factory at about 2 p.m. 12.6.36 at the same time
as the factory master's wife, who came accompanied by several
male Chinese with the intention of removing the machinery.
Seeing the detective on the scene, the workers came to the
conclusion that he was there for the express purpose of intimi-
dating them to allow the machinery to be removed.
It was explained to the above named workers that C.D.S. 224
was only there, on the instructions of the undersigned, in a
neutral capacity, to see that no trouble arose between the two
parties which would necessitate police action. On receiving this
explanation the two workers stated that they were satisfied with
same, and later left the station.

Under the cloak of registering workers, the Hoong Shing (鸿兴) Hosiery Works, Rue du Marche, French Concession, suspended operations at the end of June. Copy from Daily Report of Officer in charge of Dixwell Road Police Station.
Sunday, 23rd., August, 1936.

TROUBLE WITH
COOLIES IN
HONGKEW PARK.

Further to report on Daily State of 22nd., inst., at
3.30.p.m. 22-8-36 a telephone message was received from Mr.
Repas, Hongkew Park Keeper, stating that he was expecting
trouble in Hongkew Park. A party of Police attended and
ascertained that 50 coolies who had been employed in the
Park during the forenoon had failed to restart work at 2.p.m.
and were gathered in Chapel, opposite to the West Gate of the
Park. Coolie No.10 Lee Mo Dee and about 30 other coolies
casually employed in the Park had proceeded during the
morning to the Head Office of the P.W.D. and Coolie No.10
together with Coolie No.79 Zung Kyung San had interviewed
Mr. Kerr, Supt. of Parks and Open Spaces and complained that
Coolie No.10 had been assaulted by Mr. Repas on the 21st.
inst, and that this was the only reason for ceasing work.
They made no demands. Mr. Kerr told them to return to work
and that they would receive full pay for the day and that he
would enquire into their complaint. They returned to the
Park to work but allege Mr. Repas informed them that they
would not be required till Monday the 24th. inst. Mr. Repas
states that when they returned he told them they could start
and receive full pay for the day but instead he alleges they
intimidated 50 other coolies working in the Park and they too
ceased work. Foreman Kuh Kung Kung corroborated the state-
ments of Coolies No.10 and 79, thus contradicting that of
Mr. Repas.
Mr. Kerr was present and after negotiations Coolie
No.10 was severely cautioned re any attempt of intimidation
and was instructed to tell the other coolies to report for
work on the morning of the 23rd. inst, and to leave the
matter of the alleged assault to be dealt with by Mr. Kerr.
Coolie No.10 agreed to this and the few coolies gathered
opposite the West Gate of the Park dispersed without causing
any trouble.

demanded an explanation from complainant as to why he engaged the
two men without having first consulted them, complainant replying
that they should take no interest in the business considering that
they are employees and should they be dissatisfied they could
resign.

wages each month and not keep the $1.50 they would return to
work and on Zung agreeing to their request work was resumed.
Poo Ying Woo stated that he did not wish to take action
against Zung, but requested the police to caution him re assault-

Subject Labour situation at the Shanghai No.6 Mill (woollen factory) at
45 Chinchow Road.

Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [签名] Inspt. O. i/c

Sir,

At 1 p.m. 10/11/36 information was received from the above
mill to the effect that they were having trouble with workers
of all departments of the mill. D.S.I. Crighton and J.D.S. 42
Uecka immediately proceeded to this factory, where on arrival
enquiries revealed that at 12noon all departments had ceased
work for purpose of partaking of their mid-day meal and that
instead of commencing work at 12.30 p.m. they refused to do so.
The management then called together several of the foremen
who informed them that the workers were making the following
demands:-
(1) That the management revive the reward for non-absence.
(2) That the management make a rice allowance for the workers.
These demands were, prior to 1931 issued to all workers
employed by Japanese mills, but owing to the business depression
were cut out.
In reply to these demands the management gave the understand-
ing that they would be given due consideration and requested
workers to continue.
Work was commenced at 1 p.m. and since then the general
situation in this mill has remained normal.
At 6 p.m. 10/11/36 the night shift consisting 70 workers
paraded for duty as usual, and nothing of an outstanding nature
has since taken place.

Date June 30, 1937.
Subject Shanghai Municipality Galvanized Ironsheet Shop
Owners' Association - disturbance during inaugural
meeting in Ningpo Fellow Countrymen' Association.
Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Loyne S.S.I.

At 3.30 p.m. June 28, the Shanghai Municipality
Galvanized Ironsheet Shop Owners' Association, No.89 Heng
Meu Li, Boulevard de Montigny, which is in possession of
permit No.596 issued by the Bureau of Social Affairs, held
an inaugural meeting in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association, 480 Yu Ya Ching Road. About 300 persons,
including representatives from the local Chinese Chamber of
Commerce, the local Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs
were present, and Mr. Dzien Yung-nyi (錢永宜), owner of
the Yung Chong (永昌) Galvanized Ironsheet Shop, Miao Deu
(苗頭), Chapei, and principal of the Yoong Tsing (勇進)
Primary School, 36 Chung An Li (長安里), Tiendong Road,
presided over the meeting.

When the meeting passed the revised regulations of
the association and the scale of membership fees, one of the
promoters of the association named Tsang Ching-loong (張金龍),
who is on the list of candidates for the executive committee,
had a quarrel with two of the attendance, whom he approached
with the request to have him elected member of the executive
committee. The majority of the attendance became indignant
over this action on the part of Tsang and shouted "beat him"
thereupon Tsang took refuge on the platform. Through the
intervention of the members of the presidium, he was allowed
to go. The meeting then dispersed as more than half of the
attendance left the premises during the disturbance.

Tsang Ching-loong is the owner of the Tsang Van-
tsung Galvanized Ironsheet Shop, opposite the Yangchow Guild,
Poo Zoen Road, Chapei.
